title: Removing inhomogeneous broadening in cross-relaxation spectra via hole burning
authors: Fei Kong, Zhehua Huang, Zhengze Zhao, Pengju Zhao, Zhecheng Wang, Ya Wang, Fazhan Shi
abstract: Quantum relaxometry based on nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond is an easy-to-use technique that detects magnetic noise by measuring the longitudinal relaxation of NV centers. It is favored in chemical and biological applications due to the robustness against imperfect spin control. By tuning the energy level, NV relaxometry can detect magnetic noise generated by other spins and obtain magnetic resonance spectra through cross relaxation. However, the inhomogeneous broadening of NV centers greatly limits the spectral resolution of cross-relaxation spectra. Here we demonstrate a hole-burning technique to remove the inhomogeneous broadening. We utilize a weak pump field to deplete specific NV centers during the relaxation measurement, which contribute a reverse signal in the cross-relaxation spectra with a much narrower linewidth. Our method retains the convenience and sensitivity of NV relaxometry, opening up new avenues for high-resolution magnetic resonance spectroscopy in complex scenarios.
summary: The paper introduces and experimentally validates a hole-burning technique to overcome inhomogeneous broadening in cross-relaxation spectra measured using NV centers in diamond. By selectively depleting specific sensor states, the method dramatically improves spectral resolution, enabling the clear spectroscopic identification of weakly coupled nuclear spins like $^{19}	ext{F}$ and ${}^1	ext{H}$. This advancement enhances the utility of NV magnetometry for high-resolution studies in complex materials.
main_problem: Inhomogeneous broadening significantly limits the spectral resolution of cross-relaxation spectra obtained using Nitrogen-Vacancy (NV) centers in diamond for magnetic noise detection.
main_result: A hole-burning technique successfully removes inhomogeneous broadening, allowing the clear resolution of distinct nuclear spin frequencies ($^{19}	ext{F}$ and ${}^1	ext{H}$) that were previously unresolved.
method: The authors adapted an optical hole-burning technique by applying a weak pump RF field during cross-relaxation measurements to selectively deplete specific NV centers, creating narrow spectral features.
model_or_system: The system utilizes Nitrogen-Vacancy (NV) centers in diamond as quantum sensors for magnetic noise detection. The measurement relies on cross-relaxation spectroscopy between the NV center and target nuclear spins ($^{19}	ext{F}$, ${}^1	ext{H}$).
key_observables: Cross-relaxation spectrum $S(\omega)$, hole-burning linewidth ($	ext{FWHM}_{	ext{HB}}$), and contrast of the burned holes.
important_parameters: Dephasing rate ($\Gamma^{*}_2$), coherence rate ($\Gamma_2$), weak pump field strength ($b_2$), and resonance frequencies (e.g., $1.446\ 	ext{MHz}$ for $^{19}	ext{F}$).
main_assumptions: The method retains the convenience of NV relaxometry while improving spectral resolution; approximations are used in deriving theoretical spectra.
figures_summary: Figure 2 compares initial cross-relaxation spectra (broad) with hole-burning spectra (narrow, resolving two distinct peaks for $^{19}	ext{F}$ and ${}^1	ext{H}$). Figure 3 shows the dependence of the burned linewidth on pump strength ($b_2$).
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the limitation posed by inhomogeneous broadening in NV cross-relaxation. It then details the hole-burning methodology, demonstrating its application to resolve specific nuclear spin frequencies experimentally. Finally, it compares this technique's performance against other advanced sensing methods.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful spectroscopic tool for quantum sensors, directly addressing spectral limitations inherent in solid-state quantum platforms by adapting techniques from atomic physics (hole burning) to measure local magnetic environments with high fidelity.
